## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

ProfileViewModel — app-phone/src/main/java/com/mgilli/hyroxtracker/ui/profile/ProfileViewModel.kt

## Trigger

Any of the four settings fields (HR max, the four zone thresholds, expected
distance, long-press duration) losing focus, already wired through
`onFocusChanged` in ProfileScreen.kt to the matching ProfileViewModel
handler — observed

## Today

`onZoneThresholdChanged` already exists and already calls
`profileRepository.updateZoneThreshold(index, value)` — `ZoneThresholdField`
in ProfileScreen.kt already renders an editable field per zone (2 through 5)
and calls it on focus loss, the same way `onExpectedDistanceChanged` and
`onLongPressChanged` do for their own fields. `ProfileRepositoryImpl`'s four
updaters (`updateHrMaxBpm`, `updateZoneThreshold`, `updateExpectedDistanceM`,
`updateLongPressMs`) each return `Result.failure` with a message naming the
violated constraint when the value is out of range (or, for zone thresholds,
when the four values would no longer be strictly increasing). None of the
four ProfileViewModel handlers inspects the `Result` it receives — every
call site discards it. `ProfileUiState` carries no field for a rejection
message, and the four text fields on ProfileScreen keep their local,
just-typed value on focus loss regardless of whether the update succeeded
(their `remember(uiState.xxx)` key only changes when the stored value
changes, so a rejected value is never reverted and no message is shown).

## Expected

Losing focus on any of the four settings — the HR max dialog's confirm
included — calls its ProfileRepository updater and inspects the returned
Result. On success, nothing changes beyond what already happens. On
failure, the field's displayed value reverts to the profile's last stored
value and a short message stating the violated constraint is shown next to
that field, cleared on the next successful edit of the same field.

This requires two things the current mechanism does not carry:

- `ProfileUiState` (or an equivalent piece of per-field state) needs a slot
  to hold a rejection message per field, so ProfileScreen can render it —
  no such field exists today.
- A short, user-facing string naming each constraint (HR max range, zone
  threshold range and ordering, distance range, long-press range) needs a
  `PhoneStringResources.Profile` entry — none exists today; only the
  `IllegalArgumentException`/`IndexOutOfBoundsException` messages inside
  `ProfileRepositoryImpl` describe the constraints, and those are not
  user-facing text.
